newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1-dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct hog prices Friday were seen steady to $1.00 per cwt higher, with strength expected particularly in the eastern Corn Belt, where hog marketings were expected to be curbed by increased fieldwork, livestock dealers said.
"We'll have light receipts as long as the sun is out," an Indiana hog dealer said.
However, marketings in the western belt were seen remaining more than adequate for packer demand as most fields remain too wet for field preparation or planting, dealers there said.

At least one major packer buyer who buys hogs in central Iowa and Minnesota was said to have hogs booked for Friday's slaughter by late afternoon Thursday and would be bidding steady for Monday delivery, dealers said.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to plant Friday were seen ranging rrom $56.50 to $57.00, sources there said.

Illinois prices at plants could range $55.50 to $56.00, with possible premiums of $1.00 to $2.00 paid by packers tight on live inventory, buyers said. Indiana/Ohio top prices at plants could range $55.00-$56.00, sources there said.
